strongest_reason: Low willingness to pay (2/5) indicates users are not accustomed to paying for a dedicated template management tool, and the economic impact of the pain is moderate (3/5), making monetization highly uncertain.
strongest_risk: Feature absorption by existing CPaaS platforms (Twilio, WATI, Interakt) who can add rejection reason dashboards or category alerts as minor updates, leveraging their existing customer base and API integration.
unresolved_assumption: Whether users would actually pay for a third-party template management tool given the free manual workaround (spreadsheets, support tickets) and the skepticism that a third party can surface better data than Meta provides natively.
recommended_next_step: Discard this opportunity; consider monitoring Meta's WhatsApp Manager for UI improvements that could reduce the pain, or revisit if a low-cost freemium model with deep BSP integration can be validated through direct customer interviews.
